_what: Serving arms of the Olala quantization study as data. serve_olala.sh turns one entry into a `vllm serve` command through arms.py. Every flag below was read in the fork's source (OVHai-LLM/vllm, branch olala-v0.33, commit ebbadef, recon/src/vllm); confirmed_flags gives the file and line. Nothing here is invented.
ignore_source: recon/quantizability.md section C.2 (Appendix C of the OVH report: Mamba-3 layers 1, 7, 23 and MoE layers 0, 1, 5, 19). fnmatch patterns: should_ignore_layer(use_fnmatch=True) in online/base.py:301-307, so '*' matches dots. NOTE: PROTOCOL.md section 2 says 'down projections of the MoE blocks'; mlp.* is broader (the whole block of those four layers).

confirmed_flags.--quantization-config: vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:994; schema QuantizationConfigArgs in vllm/config/quantization.py:111 (linear, moe, ignore, targets)
confirmed_flags.--gpu-memory-utilization: vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1389 (only through the extra flags after --)

bf16.description: Reference: the BF16 checkpoint, no quantization (B0 of PROTOCOL.md).
bf16.source: model card 'vllm serve' block plus --max-num-seqs 256 (PROTOCOL.md section 3)

fp8pc.description: Online FP8, per-channel weight scale and dynamic per-token activation (llm-compressor FP8_DYNAMIC shape); F1 of PROTOCOL.md. Name without suffix = with the ignore list.

fp8pt.description: Online FP8, one weight scale per tensor.

fp8pb.description: Online FP8, 128x128 block weight scales and 1x128 block activation scales.
fp8pb.source: vllm/config/quantization.py:200-203 (fp8_per_block -> kFp8Static128BlockSym); block 128 divides 1536, 384, 768, 3072, 4608 (recon section D.3)

mxfp4.description: Online MXFP4 (OCP microscaling FP4, e8m0 scale per 32 elements) on linears and routed experts.
mxfp4.source: vllm/config/quantization.py:214-217; online/mxfp4.py (input size divisible by 32: holds for every Olala dimension). Deferred shorthand (quantization.py:238): online only because the BF16 checkpoint has no quantization metadata. Backend per GPU not confirmed.

nvfp4pt.description: Online NVFP4 (FP4 e2m1, group-16 FP8 scales, per-token activation scales) on the routed experts only: linears stay BF16 in this method; N2 of PROTOCOL.md. Needs an SM100 (B200) GPU.
nvfp4pt.source: vllm/config/quantization.py:222-226 (moe only); online/nvfp4.py:100-103 raises unless current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100): the RTX PRO 4500 and 6000 (sm_120) are refused

mxfp8.description: Extra, not in PROTOCOL.md: online MXFP8. W8A8 needs SM100+, other GPUs run W8A16.

int8wo.description: Extra, not in PROTOCOL.md: INT8 weight-only on the routed experts, the path OVH built kernels and a loader for (W8A16).

ckpt.description: An offline checkpoint directory (llm-compressor FP8 or NVFP4, GPTQ, AWQ): served with the common flags and no --quantization; vLLM reads quantization_config from the directory's config.json. The fork's load_weights does not load such checkpoints without a patch (recon section D.4): read the log for 'not found, skipping'.

unconfirmed: Which MoE and linear backend each online scheme selects on sm_89, sm_90, sm_100 and sm_120 (oracle code not traced).
Whether non-gated ReLU^2 routed experts run on the FP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 MoE kernels of every GPU (CutlassExpertsFp8Base does not support them, recon section D.2).
Whether the Olala-specific MoE decode kernels are lost with any quant_config (recon section D.3): decode speed of quantized arms may be below BF16.
The 'Quantizing N layers of types' summary line (model_loader/base_loader.py:152) is the only log proof that the ignore list took effect.
Memory: --max-num-seqs 256 with float32 SSM state on 24 to 32 GB cards; tune --gpu-memory-utilization after the first start.
